- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/claude-issue-dispatch.md:line 46 | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The failure reply uses a single message ("blocker comment not posted") for two distinct failure modes — label write failure or comment write failure. When only adding `ai:claude-blocked` fails but the comment POST succeeds, the reply says the comment was not posted even though it is visible on the issue.
  WHY: An operator or the pickup's wake report sees "blocker comment not posted" as the reason, checks the issue, finds a visible comment, and concludes the message was wrong — eroding trust in the failure path's accuracy. The operational impact is negligible because the comment itself carries the `/reclarify` instruction and the issue is correctly blocked.

- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/claude-issue-dispatch.md:lines 46-48 (the launch-prompt failure branch); same text in .claude/commands/claude-issue-dispatch.md at lines 46-48 | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The failure-branch reply uses the suffix `(label check failed; blocker comment not posted)` whenever EITHER the `ai:claude-blocked` label add OR the comment post fails. When only the label add fails (the comment still posts), the reply still says the blocker comment was not posted even though the `<!-- ai:claude-blocked:v1 -->` comment IS visible on the issue.
  WHY: Pickup logs that grep for `blocker comment not posted` to triage stuck issues will see false positives — a target whose `ai:claude-blocked` label never made it on but whose marker comment is on the issue will be reported as "comment not posted". Operators investigating a stuck issue cannot distinguish "label failed" from "comment failed" from this single reply string. The test `tests/test_implement_issue_claude_command.py::test_dispatched_session_stops_when_the_claim_was_removed` only asserts on the order of the three branches in the prompt and the literal presence of the failure text; it does not exercise the per-call attribution, so this regression ships unguarded.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

- .claude/commands/claude-issue-dispatch.md:line 46, the parenthetical `issue not started (label check failed; blocker comment not posted)` when the label or the comment call failed | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The failure-reply message conflates two distinct failure modes. If the label write fails but the comment POST succeeds, the reply claims the blocker comment was not posted even though it is visible on the issue.
  WHY: The two writes are independent REST calls; each can fail on its own. The reply string does not distinguish which one failed, so it can misreport the comment's state. This is a display-only inaccuracy (no state corruption), but it could mislead an operator into reposting a comment that already exists or missing a comment that is present.
